title: A quasi-compact open of a base change X_A is defined over a finitely generated subalgebra
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $X$ be a scheme over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base] and let $A$ be a commutative $k$-algebra. For a $k$-subalgebra $A'\subseteq A$ write $X_{A'}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}A'$ and $X_A=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}A$ for the base changes [def-pc-base-change], and $\pi:X_A\to X_{A'}$ for the morphism $\mathrm{id}_X\times\operatorname{Spec}(A'\hookrightarrow A)$ induced by the inclusion [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $V\subseteq X_A$ be a quasi-compact open subset. Then there are a $k$-subalgebra $A'\subseteq A$ that is finitely generated as a $k$-algebra and a quasi-compact open subset $V'\subseteq X_{A'}$ such that $V=\pi^{-1}(V')$. (No separatedness or quasi-separatedness of $X$ is assumed.)

proof.text: Let P(U) mean that U is the inverse image of a compact open over a finitely generated subalgebra. The empty open satisfies P using the bottom subalgebra and the empty descended open.

P is closed under binary unions: for coefficient algebras B and C use B sup C, which is finitely generated. Pull both compact opens back along X_(B sup C) to X_B and X_C; these morphisms are quasi-compact because maps between affine spectra are affine and this property is stable under base change. Their union is compact. Functoriality of baseChangeMap and preimage_sup identify its inverse image with the original union. The Lean proof establishes projection composition and quasi-compactness explicitly.

For each x in V use [lem-weil-pbc-descended-qc-neighborhood] to choose an open U_x with P(U_x), containing x and contained in V. Compactness of V gives a finite subcover. Finset induction using the empty case and binary-union case gives P of its union. The cover and containment prove that union equals V. Unpack P and take the canonical baseChangeMap as the required projection.
